A Russian national who assisted in the occupation of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) has been appointed IAEA Deputy Director General for Nuclear Energy. Despite calls from international organizations and Ukraine’s categorical opposition, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi has appointed Alexey Ferapontov, deputy head of Russia’s nuclear regulatory body Rostekhnadzor, as his deputy and head of the IAEA’s Department of Nuclear Energy, The Moscow Times reports. Grossi claimed that the decision was based on Ferapontov’s professional qualifications, adding that the official’s nationality was of no concern to him. Ferapontov is expected to assume the new role in early 2027. Roman Ustinov, Deputy Permanent Representative of the Russian Federation to international organizations in Vienna, told the Russian state news agency TASS that the IAEA’s Department of Nuclear Energy has been headed by representatives of the USSR or Russia since the organization was founded. Notably, Rostekhnadzor illegally issued an operating license for the Ukrainian nuclear power plant currently occupied by Russian forces. In 2024, Ferapontov visited the ZNPP on a “working visit.” The Russian official has been under Ukrainian sanctions since February 2023.
